overall: The AG found the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by not approving its February 17, 2021 minutes timely, declined intentional-violation and broad-audit claims, and ordered future compliance; no further remedy since minutes were approved.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to timely approve the minutes of its February 17, 2021 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: For the reasons stated above, we find that the Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to approve the minutes of its February 17, 2021, meeting in a timely manner.

allegations.summary: Complainant urged a finding that the untimely approval of the minutes was an intentional violation.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to find, as the Complainant urges, that this violation was intentional.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that, in general, the Board fails to post its meeting minutes online.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law where the Open Meeting Law does not require that minutes be posted to a website; therefore, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that, in general, the Board fails to timely approve its meeting minutes across meetings.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review this allegation as our office will not conduct broad audits of a public body.

allegations.summary: Allegations raised in the request for further review were not reviewed by the AG.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we also decline to review the allegations raised in the request for further review.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
